A1.justification: Both 12-page PDFs describe the same OmniVCus work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original video-generation evaluations, a 37-participant user study, and ablation results in Tables 1–2 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original quantitative evaluations, user-study outcomes, ablations, and qualitative results reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same VideoCus-Factory pipeline, DiT architecture, Lottery Embedding, Temporally Aligned Embedding, IVTM training, and flow-matching objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training sources and cover the same single- and multi-subject customization, instructive editing, camera control, mask control, and depth control scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator membership: VideoBooth, DreamVideo, Wan2.1-I2V, and SkyReels-A2 in the corresponding subject/editing comparisons, and Motionctrl, Cameractrl, and CamI2V for camera control. OmniGen-based combinations are unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 report identical training budgets, preprocessing, input resolutions, evaluation sample counts, five evaluation metrics, and user-study procedures.

E4.justification: Table 2 and Figure 9 retain the same filtering, augmentation, embedding, and mixed-training ablations, together with the same zero-shot multi-subject and misaligned-control analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point scores and user-preference percentages. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and rankings in Tables 1–2 are identical. The qualitative examples in Figures 1–2 and 5–9 and their reported findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), including the Lottery Embedding sampling rule, TAE mapping, and flow-matching formulation, are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain identical claims about multi-subject customization, multimodal control, instructive editing, and superiority to the evaluated baselines.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 retain the same explanations of identity preservation, subject composition, embedding failures, and texture transfer under misaligned controls. No new limitations or qualifications are introduced.

D1.justification: Implementation and access information are unchanged, including the 5B-parameter model, 100K training steps, batch size 356, 64 A100 GPUs, optimizer settings, augmentation details, and project-page link.

R1.justification: Section 2, the comparisons with prior research, and all 78 reference entries are identical. No cited works or research-positioning claims are added or removed.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 29 June 2025 to v2 dated 11 October 2025, with its self-link updated accordingly. All paper prose, author information, terminology, and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: All nine figures, both tables, captions, and page layouts are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–12 match exactly; page 1 differs only in the version/date-stamp characters.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves v1's scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and body presentation. The only identified update is the arXiv version/date stamp and associated self-link, which does not meaningfully alter paper quality.
